terms.title: Terms of service
short: FIG is free for you, and there are no ads for now.
A deal counts once staff scan your QR at the restaurant.
One account per person. No sharing codes or faking visits.

sections.heading: 1. Who we are
paragraphs: FIG is a local deals app based in Markham, Ontario, Canada, run by Brendan Lau ("FIG", "we", "us"). These terms cover the FIG app and website. By creating an account, you agree to them and to our Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: 2. Your account
paragraphs: You can look around FIG without an account. To claim deals, order or post, you need one, and you must be 14 or older. If you're under 18, check with a parent or guardian that it's okay. Use your real name, an email (confirmed with a code) and a mobile number (confirmed with a text code once texts are switched on). One account per person, and a confirmed mobile number belongs to one account. Keep your password private. You can turn on two-step sign-in (an authenticator app, a code by email, or a code by text message). Restaurant owners and managers need it for money steps like payouts and refunds. You're responsible for what happens on your account.

sections.heading: 3. How deals work
paragraphs: Deals are offered by restaurants, not by FIG. Each deal shows its own rules (times, limits, dine-in only, and so on) before you claim it.
• A claimed deal is yours until the restaurant ends the deal, or until a flash or dated deal is over.
• At the restaurant, open your QR code. It doesn't change with time: a code works once, and if the deal can be used more than once, your screen shows a new code after each scan.

• The deal is used when staff scan your code. That scan is a "redemption". A restaurant can let one claim be used more than once (up to 20 times) and can set a wait between uses; your claim shows how many uses are left and when the next one is ready.

• Each deal can be claimed once per person per day, whether you claim it or order it as takeout. Scans of one claim on the same day count as one visit. If you pay for a takeout order after you've already used its deal that day, the order is declined and your card isn't charged.

Restaurants can change or end a deal at any time. A deal isn't guaranteed until staff scan it. Some deals come as takeout: a takeout order comes with a deal, which is applied to it, unless the restaurant sets 0 deals per order, then it is at full price; dine-in only deals can't be. You pay the restaurant in the app. If you don't collect an order within 2 hours of its pickup time, it shows as a missed pickup on your takeout record (12 months), which restaurants can see when you order. Nobody reports it and takeout is never switched off for it.

sections.heading: 4. Play fair
paragraphs: Restaurants honour every deal in good faith, so we protect them from abuse. Don't:
• make more than one account
• share, screenshot or sell QR codes
• fake visits or redeem without buying
• use bots, scripts or location spoofing
• harass restaurant staff or other diners
If we see this, we may cancel claims or suspend your account.

sections.heading: 5. Restaurants and your food
paragraphs: FIG doesn't run any restaurant. Food, prices, service, safety and allergens are the restaurant's responsibility. Dietary filters are a guide only. Always tell staff about allergies before you order.

sections.heading: 6. What you send us
paragraphs: If you send us photos, reports or feedback, you still own them. You let us use them to run and improve FIG. Don't send anything that isn't yours or breaks the law. Reviews must be about your own scanned visit and honest. They're public under your first name and last initial. We can remove reviews that are abusive, fake or off-topic.

sections.heading: 7. Leaving FIG
paragraphs: You can delete your account anytime in Profile → Account & password. We can suspend or close accounts that break these terms. If we do, we'll tell you why unless the law or safety stops us.

When you delete your account, restaurants keep their records of your orders and visits without your name. You can choose to keep a way to bring them back if you return within 12 months; see the Privacy policy.

sections.heading: 8. Our responsibility
paragraphs: We work hard to keep FIG accurate and running, but it's provided "as is". As far as the law allows, we aren't liable for indirect losses, and our total liability to you is limited to the greater of what you paid us in the last 12 months or $50 CAD. Nothing here removes your rights under Ontario consumer protection law.

sections.heading: 9. Changes to these terms
paragraphs: If we make an important change, we'll tell you in the app at least 14 days before it starts. If you keep using FIG after that, the new terms apply.

sections.heading: 10. Governing law
paragraphs: These terms are governed by the laws of Ontario and the federal laws of Canada that apply there. Disputes go to the courts of Ontario.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
short: We collect what we need to show you deals nearby and check that redemptions are real.
We never sell your personal information.
Restaurants only see what they need to verify your visit.
Location is used while you use FIG, and for alerts only if you turn them on.
You can download or delete your data anytime.
If you delete your account, restaurants keep their order and visit records without your name.

sections.heading: 1. Who's responsible
paragraphs: FIG, based in Markham, Ontario, Canada, is responsible for your personal information. We follow Canada's privacy law (PIPEDA). Our Privacy Officer, Brendan Lau, answers questions sent with Message us in the app, or from the contact page at www.figpromo.ca/contact.

sections.heading: 2. What we collect
paragraphs: • Account: name, username, email (confirmed with a code), mobile number (we'll confirm it with a text code once texts are switched on), photo, and your password (stored scrambled, never readable).
• Taste: cravings, budget, dietary needs and home area from Profile setup.

• Location: your precise location while you use FIG, to show nearby deals. It's optional: you can find, claim and use every deal with it off. If you tap I'm here on a takeout order, we keep how far you were from the restaurant with that order. If you turn on arrival reminders, also when you arrive at a restaurant where you have a claimed deal.
• Activity: claims, verified visits, searches, takeout orders, and the reviews and photos you post.
• Device: phone model, app version, notification token and crash reports.
• Terms: which version of our terms you accepted, and when.

• Two-step sign-in: if you turn it on, the key that links FIG to your authenticator app (the codes it makes stay on your phone), or the email address or mobile number we send codes to. When we send you a code we keep only a scrambled copy of it for 10 minutes. Backup codes are kept scrambled too.
• Support: messages and reports you send us.

• Payments (restaurants): a permanent record of each payment made through FIG: amounts, HST, FIG's fee, Stripe's fee, order numbers, dates and Stripe reference numbers. It has no card numbers, names or emails.
• Team invitations: the email address a restaurant invites, the role, and when the invite ends.

• How you found FIG: the tag on the link you came from (a creator’s link or a flyer’s QR code, for example), noted once when you join the waitlist, sign up or add a restaurant, and your answer to “How did you hear about FIG?” if you give one (you can skip it). We use them only to see which outreach works. Restaurants never see them.

• In your browser: your sign-in and the app's saved state (so you stay signed in), which link brought you to FIG (until you close the tab), whether FIG is open to diners, and an offline copy of the website's pages. No advertising cookies. If you accept, Google Analytics sets cookies for up to 2 years; if you decline, it sets none. Vercel Web Analytics sets no cookies.

sections.heading: 3. How we use it
paragraphs: • Show deals and places near you
• Verify redemptions and stop fraud
• Keep a record of your visits, so you can rate them and find places again
• Personalise Home (you can turn this off)
• Send the alerts and emails you chose
• Emails about deals and FIG news only if you said yes when you signed up. Each one has an unsubscribe link, and you can turn them off anytime in Account & password
• Answer support requests and improve FIG
FIG doesn't show ads for now. We don't sell your information or show you third-party ads based on it.

sections.heading: 4. Dietary needs
paragraphs: Dietary needs can say something about your health or beliefs, so we treat them as sensitive. They're only used to filter places and deals for you, and they're never shared, with restaurants or anyone else.

sections.heading: 5. What restaurants see
paragraphs: When staff scan your QR, the restaurant sees your first name and last initial, the deal, and the time. Their dashboard shows totals, like "42 redemptions this week", not who you are. Restaurants never see your email or location. When you order takeout, they see how many of your takeout orders in the last 12 months you picked up or missed, nothing else. They never see your mobile number, not even for a takeout order: they reach you only through FIG, for example "We're waiting" on a takeout order. Reviews you post are public and show your first name and last initial.

sections.heading: 6. Companies that help us
paragraphs: These companies process data for us, only to run FIG, under contracts that protect it:
• Supabase: database and sign-in
• Vercel: hosting, and anonymous visit counts for the website (Vercel Web Analytics: no cookies, no personal profile)
• Google Analytics: website visit statistics (pages viewed, approximate location, device type), using cookies only if you accept them; see the Cookies page
• Resend: sends FIG's emails, so it gets your email address and what the email says

• Stripe: card payments for takeout orders, and restaurants’ payouts. To set up a restaurant’s payouts, FIG shares its business name, address, phone and email with Stripe. ID and bank details go straight to Stripe and never pass through FIG.
• Twilio: text messages, like codes that confirm your mobile number or sign you in, once we switch texts on
• Komoot (Photon): the address search when you or a restaurant look up an address. What you type, and your internet address, go to its servers in Germany
• OpenFreeMap (map tiles), jsDelivr (code the pages load) and Unsplash (some pictures on Home): they see your internet address, as any website does, so they can send it
• Apple and Google: sign-in, maps, notifications

sections.heading: 7. Where your data lives
paragraphs: Some of these companies store data outside Canada, mostly in the United States. There, it's protected by our contracts but also covered by local law. Address searches go to Komoot in Germany, where the European Union's privacy law applies.

sections.heading: 8. How long we keep it
paragraphs: We keep your data while your account is open. When you delete your account, we erase your personal information within 30 days, and it's gone from our backup copies within 60 days.

Restaurants keep the records of your takeout orders and visits for their tax and accounting records, for as long as they're on FIG. Payments are also recorded by Stripe, our payment processor. When you delete your account, your name on those records is replaced with "Former diner", and your notes on dishes and your distance from the restaurant are removed.

If you tick "Keep a way to bring back my past visits and orders" when you delete, we also keep a one-way code made from your email (not the email itself) for 12 months. If you sign up again with the same confirmed email in that time, you can choose to bring back those orders and visits, or start fresh, which deletes the saved link. Your saved places, claims and reviews can't come back. If you don't tick it, the records can't be linked to you again.

Payment records of takeout and plan payments made through FIG are kept for 7 years, for tax and accounting, and stay after an account is closed. They hold no name, email or card number. An email address that a restaurant invited is deleted within 60 days after the invite ends.

sections.heading: 9. Your choices
paragraphs: • See or fix your info in Profile
• Download it in Privacy & terms
• Turn off location, alerts or personalised picks
• Delete your account at any time
• No account (on the waitlist, or you wrote to us)? Ask for a copy of your information, a correction or its deletion through the contact page (choose Privacy or my data). We answer within 30 days
Not happy with our answer? You can complain to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada.

sections.heading: 10. Keeping it safe
paragraphs: We encrypt data in transit, scramble passwords and limit who on our team can access data. You can turn on two-step sign-in, so signing in also needs a code from an authenticator app, an email or a text message. Where it's available, you can sign in with a code we text to your confirmed mobile number instead of a password. No system is perfect. If a breach could put you at risk, we'll tell you and the Privacy Commissioner, as the law requires.

sections.heading: 11. Age
paragraphs: FIG is for people 14 and older. We don't knowingly collect information from anyone younger. If we learn that someone under 14 has an account, we delete it.

sections.heading: 12. Changes
paragraphs: If we change how we use your information in an important way, we'll tell you in the app first, and ask for your consent where the law requires it.

business-terms.title: Business terms
short: One plan covers all your restaurants (up to 2 for now): $29.99 a month or $299.99 a year from the day FIG opens to diners, before tax (before then, founding restaurants can pay $49.99 once instead). Your page, deals and scans are included, with no commission on the bill.
Takeout orders paid in the app: FIG keeps 5% of the food, and Stripe’s card fee comes off the same payment.
Honour your live deals exactly as written.
Only you and the staff you invite can verify a deal.

sections.heading: 1. Who these terms are for
paragraphs: These terms apply to restaurants in Canada that use FIG Business. They sit alongside our Terms of service and Privacy policy. By signing up, you confirm you're 18 or older and can accept them for your business.

sections.heading: 2. Your listing
paragraphs: You must run a real, licensed food business at the address you give us, and keep your details accurate. Setting up is free. Your page and deals go live when your plan does (the founding payment before FIG opens to diners) and your page has at least one photo. We can pause or remove a listing that breaks these terms.

sections.heading: 3. Your deals
paragraphs: You choose your deals, times and daily limits. While a deal is live, you must honour it exactly as listed. Don't raise prices to cancel out a discount. If you pause a deal, keep honouring claims made before that. Ending a deal is what stops its claims.
• You can let a diner use a deal more than once (up to 20 times) and set a wait between uses. Each claim keeps the rules it was made with.

sections.heading: 4. What FIG costs
paragraphs: • One plan covers all of your locations, now and later (up to 2 for now): their pages, going live, posting deals and verified scans. It's $29.99 a month or $299.99 a year from the day FIG opens to diners, before tax. Signing up and setting up your listing are free; going live, deals, scanning and takeout need a plan. There's no commission on the bill, and no per-scan or per-listing fees.

• Founding restaurants: before FIG opens to diners, you can pay $49.99 once. It covers your plan, for all your restaurants, until FIG starts billing. FIG will tell you that date, and your founding price, in writing at least 14 days before. From then, you can keep your plan at a founding price that is always lower than FIG's regular price, for as long as your plan stays active; if you don't, your plan ends on that date. Refunds: within 14 days of paying, and in full if FIG hasn't opened to diners by March 1, 2027 (before billing has started).
• FIG plans to open to diners on January 1, 2027. FIG can't promise how many diners you'll get. Prices are before tax, plus HST once FIG is registered.

• Regular plans: refunds within 14 days of your first payment. Your card is charged automatically each month or year until you cancel in FIG's Settings. Cancelling stops the renewal, and you keep full access until the end of the month or year you've paid. Nothing else is refundable.
• The refund you can ask for yourself in FIG is once per owner. If you've had a refund before, a later one is FIG's to give: message us.
• Stripe processes the plan's payments. FIG never sees your card number.

• Takeout orders paid in the app are paid out to you through Stripe. Setting up payouts happens inside FIG, and accepting Stripe’s terms (the Stripe Connected Account Agreement) is part of it. Your ID and bank details go straight to Stripe, never to FIG.

• When a diner pays for a takeout order in the app, FIG keeps 5% of the food after the deal’s discount, before tax, and Stripe’s card fee (2.9% + $0.30 for most Canadian cards; cards from outside Canada cost more) comes off the same payment. The rest, tax included, is paid out to you, and the tax is yours to remit.
• If you refund an order, in full or in part, FIG gives back its fee in proportion. Stripe keeps its card fee.
• FIG isn’t registered for HST yet. Once it is, it will add 13% HST to its plan and its 5% fee, and we’ll tell you at least 30 days before that starts.
• Your plan includes everything FIG offers restaurants. If we ever offer a paid extra, we'll show the price and what's included before you buy anything.
• Your payments: every takeout payment, refund and fee, and your plan payments, are listed under Payments, where you can download them as a CSV file. It is a permanent record, kept for 7 years.

sections.heading: 5. Wrong scans and disputes
paragraphs: If you think a scan is wrong, message us within 14 days. We review it, and if it was a mistake we remove it.

sections.heading: 6. Reviews
paragraphs: Paying FIG never changes, hides or removes reviews. You can reply to reviews in public. Don't offer anything in exchange for a review.

sections.heading: 7. Staff
paragraphs: You're responsible for scans made by your team. Only owners and managers can refund takeout orders. Remove access when someone leaves. People join your team only by accepting an invite you send, to one email address or by a link that expires and that you can revoke. Owners can invite managers and staff; managers can invite staff. Owners and managers need two-step sign-in turned on, and a fresh code, for money steps like payouts, refunds, plan changes, handing a restaurant over and closing it.

sections.heading: 8. Diner information
paragraphs: You'll see a diner's first name, last initial and the deal they used, never their mobile number or email. Reach a diner only through FIG (for example "We're waiting" on a takeout order), and only to serve that deal or order. Don't contact diners outside FIG, and handle their information as Canadian privacy law requires.
If a diner deletes their account, you keep your records of their orders and visits, shown as "Former diner".

sections.heading: 9. Ending the agreement
paragraphs: You can close your business account anytime. Takeout orders already paid are paid out as usual. We can suspend or close your account if you break these terms, for example by not honouring deals or faking scans. If we close it for any other reason, nothing more is charged.
Closing a location, or your business account, deletes that location's orders and visit records from FIG. Save your takeout statements first: you need them for your own tax records.

sections.heading: 10. Responsibility
paragraphs: You're responsible for your food, prices, service and safety, and for any claims about them. FIG is provided "as is". As far as the law allows, our total liability is limited to the greater of the fees you paid us in the last 12 months or $100 CAD.

sections.heading: 11. Changes and law
paragraphs: If we ever charge for something, we'll give you at least 30 days' notice first. These terms follow Ontario law, and disputes go to the courts of Ontario.
